Members have the advantage of access to more materials for training Smithing than free-to-play players. With the right methods and a bit of increased training time, members are able to make money while smithing. For tables showing profit versus experience made by smithing certain items, see Smithing/Smithing tables.

Broadly, there are three main types of Smithing training. Smelting bars is rather bad xp and profit, but has up to 144 seconds in between clicks. Making upgraded armour is good xp, and there are many strategies to boost this method, but it requires lots of starting money and lower-levelled items may not sell well. Making burial equipment sets (which destroys the armour) is among the fastest xp of any skill in the entire game and among the most expensive, at over 4 million xp / hour off Double XP under ideal conditions.

Forging items from bars is a fairly efficient method to level Smithing. To smith items, players need to click on a forge and select the target item, then use an anvil to make progress smithing it. With every swing, the heat of an item depletes; the lower the heat, the lower the progress made on the item. Therefore, players should re-heat their item by clicking the forge, wait until the heat bar is full, and continue forging on the anvil.

If higher experience rates are desired, but is too expensive, instead of forging the entire set from bars, just the last step can be forged. For example, elder rune platelegs + 4 can be upgraded to elder rune platelegs + 5. For lower level metals, this is around 50% faster, while for higher metals, it is around 90%-110% faster.

  • For experience (per hour), it does not matter which equipment piece is forged. Therefore, players concerned about the cost of Smithing should create the item with the smallest loss.
  • Forging items can be queued by opening the furnace menu again, selecting the target item and waiting until the heat bar is filled. This can be repeated until the desired number of items are queued up. By queuing items, smithing can be trained fully AFK for long periods of time.
  • If the Superheat Form curse is used, progress each swing is only decreased once the heat bar reaches 33% instead of 66%.
    • Having an grace of the elves equipped halves the prayer drain of Superheat Form.
    • The Orthen furnace core stops the prayer drain altogether, but is only available 99 Smithing and 102 Archaeology. (Both boostable)
  • Making use of a smithing autoheater or its advanced version keeps the heat between 30%-1% and 60%-1% respectively.
  • It is recommended to turn on the audio (sound effects) so that players can hear the distinct sound created by an un-heated item. This is a cue to re-heat their item.
  • Assuming all bars are purchased from the Grand Exchange and platebodies are made, the raw cost will be -1276-1605+-3797-5255+7634-8709-11698-13725 gp and after selling the created products the final profit/loss of 1-99 will be 5854-1276+11968-1605+50394-3797+137503-5255+299419-7634+1011513-8709+984845-11698+2566411-13725 gp.
  • Maximum Heat is reliant on Smithing and Firemaking. At Level 99 Smithing and Firemaking, players have a maximum heat of 894. \text{Maximum Heat} = 300 + (3 \times \text{Smithing level}) + (3 \times \text{Firemaking level}).

Using armour on a burial forge and anvil at the Artisans' Workshop will result in some of the fastest, though most expensive, Smithing experience available in the game; the products are consumed and cannot be resold for any return on investment.

  • Burial smithing is twice as fast for the same amount of experience for creating the item.
  • Only the highest tier of the item is available for use on a burial forge and anvil.
  • Although there is no additional bar cost, the item is destroyed in the process.
  • Experience rates can far exceed 1 million experience/hour depending on which item you use.
  • Smithing a full burial set grants 5% extra XP than smithing each part of the burial set individually.

You can also create a Primal burial set at 100 Smithing, currently granting the best experience rates. Combining a Primal full helm + 5, Primal platebody + 5, Primal platelegs + 5, Primal gauntlets + 5, and Primal armoured boots + 5 for a total of 282,240 experience per set. The cost per set currently totals -1855714-4168835-3248582-860733-899591 gp if all the items are purchased individually from the Grand Exchange, or -12,056,302 gp if the items are purchased as a Primal armour set + 5.The fastest and most expensive method to level smithing is to find the highest levelled armour that you can smith and then buy the fully upgraded full helm, platebody, platelegs, gauntlets, and armoured boots from the Grand Exchange and use them to create burial sets at a burial anvil and burial forge.

Smelting corrupted ore requires unlocking of Prifddinas and level 89. It requires 51,201 corrupted ore to reach level 99, or 38,642 if the full blacksmith's outfit is equipped and the Voice of Seren is active in the Trahaearn district. Each corrupted ore gives 160 base Smithing experience, or 192 Smithing experience with the Voice of Seren active. With the use of the Superheat Form curse, 2,000 corrupted ore can be used in one hour, equating to 400,000 experience an hour with the Voice of Seren effect active and the full blacksmith's outfit equipped. XP rates can be further increased with the use of other boosts such as urns.

This may be a more time-consuming method than others due to the need to mine the untradeable ore. The time mining the ore would need to be taken into consideration when looking at experience/hour rates. If you wish to use this method to bridge the 504,037 experience gap between 89 - 90 you will require 3,151 corrupted ore, 2,625 while the Voice of Seren is active, and 2,400 with the Voice of Seren active and the full blacksmith's outfit equipped.

Smelting bars is a slow but probably profitable way (except primal bars) to train Smithing, and is also highly AFK.

  • Smelting gauntlets are highly recommended because they allow players to smelt up to 60 bars at a time and reduce the clicking required by sending created bars straight to the metal bank.
  • This method is highly AFK compared to smithing platebodies, and only requires clicking every 145 seconds without smelting gauntlets (or 60 seconds with gauntlets).
  • Players will create double bars around 10% of the time earning additional profit along the way (for 2,000 input ores players will smelt around 2,200 bars) once the level required for an extra bar chance is reached.
  • The calculations below assume the player is buying ores off the Grand Exchange, bars have a 10% chance of doubling only once the extra bar chance level is reached, and the bars are sold at GE price.
  • When selling bars, it is recommended to discover the actual trading price by instant buying a single bar at a higher price, and then selling the created bars at that price instead, which will earn more profit.

The Clan Citadel can offer a furnace (provided that the clan the player is in has one), which provides constant and free Smithing experience while doing their cap rate. As players maximise their caps every week to a fealty rank of 3, they will get an extra experience bonus when skilling in the citadel. Depending on the player's fealty rank and cap limit, they can reach to upwards of 342k Smithing experience per week, more with various bonuses. However, the furnace requires charcoal from the kiln and regular/precious ore from the mine in order to function properly.

Smithing is often regarded to be a slow or expensive skill to train in free to play worlds.

Historically, smelting is slow but profitable, while smithing items yielded fast experience at significant losses. The introduction of Invention caused increased demand for many finished products. After the Mining and Smithing rework, many items can be smithed from bars at a profit, but slower than before. Smelting ore into bars still turn a profit, but gives negligible experience.

Players with low wealth should still consider the methods that favour high investment but accept that they cannot train smithing continuously (and instead must be patient with buy and sell offers), or significant loss may result.

Training while Dungeoneering is also an option, albeit integrated with combat and possibly other skills. Dungeoneering Smithing was not affected by the Mining and Smithing rework, which means smithing items is simpler and very fast in comparison and smelting bars give more experience. This is particularly the case at low levels, which are slow and tedious otherwise, and it's recommended to smith novite (the lowest tier metal) in dungeons anyway regardless of Smithing level. However, it is far more attention and input intensive, you must spend time gathering the ores yourself and no profit or usable item can be taken out of Daemonheim.

The Knight's Sword is a free-to-play quest, which requires 10 Mining but has no Smithing level requirement (10 Smithing required for the 2 Iron bars for Ironman Mode players). It is strongly recommended that players interested in Smithing, regardless of what other method preferred, complete this quest to claim a lamp, which gives 12,725 xp and allows you to skip straight to level 29. Even players with combat level 3 can do it with some food even if they are attacked by ice warriors and ice giants while mining the blurite ore.

Smithing bars into any item gives xp according to how many bars are used, e.g. each bronze bar gives 15 xp (bronze hatchet uses 1 bar and gives 15 xp; bronze 2h sword uses 4 bars and gives 60 xp). Items that takes more bars each take longer to smith, but is still slightly faster per bar, is less click intensive, and requires less banking. However, they tend to incur a loss or lower profit while there are often 1-bar items that can be smithed for more profit (starting from mithril and up, almost all items can be smithed for profit). Starting from iron, finished items can be further upgraded with more bars (up to +1 for iron and steel, +2 for mithril and adamant, and +3 for rune).

For a table showing profits versus experience made smithing certain items, see Smithing/Smithing tables.

If a player does not want to complete The Knight's sword quest, they can begin smelting copper and tin ores into bronze bars and then forging them into various bronze items. Bronze platebodies are recommended to smith due to requiring less clicking compared to other items plus they grant 75 Smithing experience. 16 bronze platebodies are required to reach level 10 Smithing.

What's Mine is Yours is a free-to-play quest requiring level 5 Smithing. It awards 400 Smithing experience upon completion, which will take a level 5 smith to level 7 immediately. The quest can be started by talking to Doric, found north of Falador. This quest involves some low-level combat, making it unsuitable for skill pures.

At level 10, players are available to forge iron bars into iron items as well as their +1 upgrades. It's best to forge bars into iron platebodies, granting 200 Smithing experience. 17 iron platebodies are required to fill 3316 Smithing experience required for level 20.

At level 20, players unlock the ability to smelt and smith steel bars 1,276 gp. To do this the following is needed:

  • 1 iron ore 551 gp
  • 1 coal 177 gp

It is recommended that you buy these ores rather than mine them (especially coal due to their low price).

It's best to forge bars into steel platebodies that grant 375 Smithing experience. 24 steel platebodies (2 if player has The Knight's Sword completed and had no Smithing experience before) are required to reach level 30.

Mithril bars can be smelted at this level, giving 5 experience. They sell for 1,605 gp in the Grand Exchange, with the mithril ore and one coal costing 643+177 gp. Roughly 1250 bars can be made per hour, for a profit of 1250*(1605-643-177) gp.

Using Superheat Item, you make a 1605-643-177-397 gp profit provided you use a fire staff and purchase the nature runes. This also allows for the most efficient use of plain smelting urns, which cost an additional 1652 per urn and fills every 25 bars. This method also lets you smelt around 1,700 bars per hour or more depending on how active you are.

For speedy skilling, it is required to smith mithril platebody and its upgrades, as they give the fastest experience before level 40.

Adamant bars can be smelted at this level, giving 7 experience. They sell for 3,797 gp in the Grand Exchange, with the adamantite ore and one luminite costing 1297+1835 gp.

At level 40 players are able to create various adamant items. Smithing adamant platebodies and its upgraded versions create high experience as well as profit (if adamant bars were made by smithers, not bought at Grand Exchange) while power skillers may choose smithing Adamant burial set in Artisans' Workshop (see experience rates at the table below).

Rune bars can be smelted at this level, giving 10 experience. They sell for 5,255 gp in the Grand Exchange, with the runite ore and one luminite costing 2754+1835 gp.

At level 50 players are available to smith various rune items as well as the most experience rewarding item in free-to-play - Rune burial set (see experience rates at the table below).

With 55 Smithing and 55 Dungeoneering, the Scroll of efficiency can be bought for 20,000 Dungeoneering tokens. After reading it, every bar you consume while smithing outside Daemonheim has a 2% chance to be saved. This offers a slight decrease in the cost of materials.

Smithing Burial equipment at Artisans' Workshop is a fast, but very expensive way to train Smithing. Smithing in the workshop also gives Respect, earning the player 1% respect every 10,000 experience while smithing, which makes it a useful training place after the early levels. Free-to-play players can buy some of the Artisans' Workshop Reward Shop rewards with respect.

With at least 59 Smithing (rune items created at full heat), rune burial set takes about 6 minutes and 45 seconds to smith without reheating, or 4 minutes and 20 seconds if reheating whenever heat falls below 60%. Taking into account the time spent withdrawing the +3 items and turning them into unfinished smithing items that can be smithed into the burial set, smithing rune burial sets yields about 170,000 xp per hour, but is very expensive.

Ideally, players strive to gain experience while making a profit. If this is not possible, then players strive to minimise the loss involved. Therefore, some calculation is necessary to determine exactly how much money is gained or lost per experience gained, and to minimise the loss or maximise the profit. This profit/loss can be calculated using the flipping calculator.

For a given bar, the price of smelting the bar can be calculated easily by adding the prices of the individual ores (optionally added to that is the price of the nature rune if Superheat Item is used). The profit/loss then is simply the price of the bar minus the cost of the materials. If the result is positive, money is gained; if it's negative, money is lost. If this value is p, then the profit or loss per experience is p/x where x is the experience gained by smelting a single bar. 1200-1400 bars may be smelted per hour depending on downtime from depositing bars and starting again.

For any given item, let n be the number of bars required to make that item. If k is the cost of one bar and x is the price of the item made, then the profit is simply x – nk. If the profit is positive, money is gained; if it is negative, money is lost. If this value is p, then the profit or loss per experience is p/e where e is the experience gained by smithing a single bar.

c.t: Profit/loss for smelting and smithing bars
c.h: For a given item, let a be the number of bars required to make that item. If b is the cost of the ores required to make one bar, and c is the price of the item made, then the profit is simply c-ab. If the profit is positive, money is gained; if it is negative, money is lost. If this value is p, then the profit or loss per experience is p/(e+f) where e is the experience gained by smithing a single item and f is the experience gained by smelting a single bar.
c.a: Profit/loss for smelting and smithing bars

c.h:
Smithing can be trained in Daemonheim, available in high complexity. Ores can be obtained from limited resources throughout a dungeon or bought with rusty coins (also gained from the dungeon) from the Smuggler. You can smelt them into bars, smith them into items then sell it back to him to recoup a small portion of the losses.

Adding a pickaxe that requires a higher level than you currently have to your tool belt will grant the best available pickaxe, thus taking the best pickaxe you can is recommended. If you have a high Smithing level, buying a high-tiered ore from the smuggler, smithing a pickaxe, and adding it to your tool belt is recommended.

However, for Smithing training, novite ore gives the best value for rusty coins as higher tier ores cost a lot more for relatively little increase in xp. This also means Dungeoneering training barely scales with level; it is extremely fast for low-level training, but slow at higher levels.

Novite two-hand swords or mauls (4 bars) are good choices. Novite platebodies (5 bars), although marginally faster, sell for the same price as 2h and mauls, thus reducing the total experience gained in each run considering capital usage.

Each ore costs 525 coins, and each maul/2h can be sold for 420 coins, or 560 with low alchemy and 840 with high alchemy. This means 20% of the cost can be recouped if selling, 40% with high alchemy without accounting for runes.

Arrowheads can also be made, as 20 arrowheads (1 bar) sell for higher as other 1-bar items. 80 novite arrowheads (4 bars) can be sold for 800 coins, nearly twice as much as one 2h/maul. This is more time consuming, but more cost effective for higher tier ores you collect in the dungeon.

Efficiency is increased slightly if High Alchemy is used, but be aware you may trade time for extra Magic and Smithing experience. A tangle gum wand or tangle gum staff can be made with 1 tangle gum branches (225 coins) at 8 Fletching and provide infinite fire runes for Alchemy spells. This is only possible in high complexity.

However, as long as any other players in the team have enabled shared experience, the Smithing experience gained will be divided equally among all the sharing players and the smelter. It is recommended to solo a dungeon to use this method.

A test at around 30-35 Mining and Smithing shows you can gain about 300-500 Mining experience and 1500-2000 Smithing experience per small, solo, high complexity dungeon (taking about 15 minutes). There may be large variations especially because every dungeon is randomly generated.
